# One-sample t-test: H₀: μ = 0 vs. H₁: μ > 0 (one-sided)

library(jsonlite)

# Parameters
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Effect size (Cohen's d)
d <- mean_diff / sd  # d = 0.4

# For a one-sample t-test with n participants (df = n-1):
# Noncentrality parameter: λ = d * sqrt(n)
# Power = P(t_{n-1, λ} > t_{crit})
# where t_{crit} is the critical value from t(df = n-1) at α = 0.05, one-sided

# Critical value for one-sided test at α = 0.05
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = Inf)  # Using normal approximation as df is large
print(paste("Critical value (one-sided, α=0.05):", round(t_crit, 4)))

# For exact calculation, we search for n where power equals or exceeds target
# Using the non-central t distribution

# Function to compute power for a given n
power_for_n <- function(n, delta, sd, alpha, type = "one.sample", alternative = "one.sided") {
  result <- stats::power.t.test(
    n = n,
    delta = delta,
    sd = sd,
    sig.level = alpha,
    type = type,
    alternative = alternative
  )
  return(result$power)
}

# Search for minimum n using binary search
n_low <- 1
n_high <- 100
tolerance <- 1e-6

while (n_high - n_low > 1) {
  n_mid <- (n_low + n_high) %/% 2
  power_mid <- power_for_n(n_mid, mean_diff, sd, alpha)
  
  if (power_mid < target_power) {
    n_low <- n_mid
  } else {
    n_high <- n_mid
  }
}

# n_high is the minimum integer n meeting target power
n_min <- n_high
power_at_min <- power_for_n(n_min, mean_diff, sd, alpha)
power_at_prev <- power_for_n(n_min - 1, mean_diff, sd, alpha)

print(paste("\n=== INDEPENDENT CHECK ==="))
print(paste("Minimum integer n:", n_min))
print(paste("Power at n =", n_min, ":", round(power_at_min, 6)))
print(paste("Power at n =", n_min - 1, ":", round(power_at_prev, 6)))
print(paste("Target power:", target_power))
print(paste("n meets target?", power_at_min >= target_power))

  type = "one.sample",

# Independent verification using explicit formulas
# One-sample t-test: H₀: μ = 0 vs. H₁: μ > 0 (one-sided)

library(jsonlite)

# Parameters
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Effect size (Cohen's d)
d <- mean_diff / sd  # d = 0.4

# For a one-sample t-test with n participants (df = n-1):
# Noncentrality parameter: λ = d * sqrt(n)
# Power = P(t_{n-1, λ} > t_{crit})
# where t_{crit} is the critical value from t(df = n-1) at α = 0.05, one-sided

# Critical value for one-sided test at α = 0.05
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = Inf)  # Using normal approximation as df is large
print(paste("Critical value (one-sided, α=0.05):", round(t_crit, 4)))

# For exact calculation, we search for n where power equals or exceeds target
# Using the non-central t distribution

# Function to compute power for a given n
power_for_n <- function(n, delta, sd, alpha, type = "one.sample", alternative = "one.sided") {
  result <- stats::power.t.test(
    n = n,
    delta = delta,
    sd = sd,
    sig.level = alpha,
    type = type,
    alternative = alternative
  )
  return(result$power)
}

# Search for minimum n using binary search
n_low <- 1
n_high <- 100
tolerance <- 1e-6

while (n_high - n_low > 1) {
  n_mid <- (n_low + n_high) %/% 2
  power_mid <- power_for_n(n_mid, mean_diff, sd, alpha)
  
  if (power_mid < target_power) {
    n_low <- n_mid
  } else {
    n_high <- n_mid
  }
}

# n_high is the minimum integer n meeting target power
n_min <- n_high
power_at_min <- power_for_n(n_min, mean_diff, sd, alpha)
power_at_prev <- power_for_n(n_min - 1, mean_diff, sd, alpha)

print(paste("\n=== INDEPENDENT CHECK ==="))
print(paste("Minimum integer n:", n_min))
print(paste("Power at n =", n_min, ":", round(power_at_min, 6)))
print(paste("Power at n =", n_min - 1, ":", round(power_at_prev, 6)))
print(paste("Target power:", target_power))
print(paste("n meets target?", power_at_min >= target_power))
print(paste("n-1 meets target?", power_at_prev >= target_power))

# Also compute continuous solution directly
result_continuous <- stats::power.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  delta = mean_diff,
  sd = sd,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

n_cont <- result_continuous$n
print(paste("\nContinuous solution (n):", round(n_cont, 4)))
print(paste("Ceiling of continuous solution:", ceiling(n_cont)))

# Verify the effect size calculation
print(paste("\nEffect size (Cohen's d):", d))
print(paste("Noncentrality at n =", n_min, ":", round(d * sqrt(n_min), 4)))

# Create comparison table
comparison <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("Continuous solution", "Minimum integer n", "Power at min n", "Power at n-1", "Meets target?"),
  candidate = c("40.0291", "41", "0.808582", "0.799738", "TRUE"),
  independent = c(round(n_cont, 4), n_min, round(power_at_min, 6), round(power_at_prev, 6), power_at_min >= target_power)
)

print("\n=== COMPARISON TABLE ===")
print(comparison)

# Final output
output <- list(
  verification = list(
    sample_size_matches = (n_min == 41),
    power_at_n_matches = (abs(power_at_min - 0.808582) < 0.00001),
    power_at_n_minus_1_matches = (abs(power_at_prev - 0.799738) < 0.00001),
    continuous_solution_matches = (abs(n_cont - 40.0291) < 0.001)
  ),
  results = list(
    sample_size = n_min,
    achieved_power = round(power_at_min, 6),
    power_at_preceding = round(power_at_prev, 6)
  )
)

cat(toJSON(output, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

  n = n_integer,
  delta = 0.2,
